summary: The root W-SH-Y primarily means to adorn or embellish something, often with various colors or patterns.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: inf. n. وَشْىٌ, He variegated, or figured, a piece of cloth, or a garment; (Mgh, Msb, * K;) and embellished it. (K.) وَشَى بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ, (S, K,) or عِنْدَ السُّلْطَانِ, (Msb,) He calumniated, or misrepresented, him to the Sultán. (S, Msb, K.)

Any colour differing from the main colour of a horse, &c.; a colour differing from the rest, (S,) or from that which generally pervades a thing. لَا شِيَةَ فِيهِ It is of one generally pervading colour, in which is no other colour. شِيَةٌ [also] A mark, sign, symptom, or token, by which a thing is known; syn. عَلَامَةٌ; (Msb;) and مَخِيلَةٌ, which see.

originally an inf. n., A kind of variegated, or figured, cloth, or garment. (Mgh, Msb. *) وَشْىٌ The variegation, figured work, or figuring, of a garment; making it partycoloured. وَشى sometimes signifies A natural diversity of colours: see رُمْلَةٌ. وَشْىٌ of a sword: see فِرِنْدٌ.
rel. n. of شِيَةٌ, the rad. و being restored; (S in the present art.;) and so, like عِدَوِىٌّ [of عِدَةٌ ]. (S in art. وعد.)
قَوْلٌ مَوْشِىٌّ بِهِ [ A saying misrepresented ]. (TA in art. قت, in an explanation of قَوْلٌ مَقْتُوتٌ.) مَوْشِىٌّ is used by Aboo-Dhu-eyb to signify A musical reed-pipe. (TA, art. نوب.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
